rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a minimum number of times a participant must perform an action within a recurring period, such as at least N actions per period: Model the task that performs this action with a label that keeps the stated minimum count and the recurring period together with the action, using the description's own quantity and period wording, so the label is not reduced to the bare action. Keep the label short and faithful to the description's wording.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a minimum number of times a participant must perform an action within a recurring period, such as at least N actions per period

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that choosing one of several alternatives, such as accepting one of several arriving alternatives, makes the other still-open alternatives void, so the choice has a consequence for the remaining ones: After the decision that selects one alternative, model an explicit task on the selected path that voids or withdraws the other still-open alternatives, placed before the process continues. Do not leave the consequence implicit, and do not model it as a flow from the decision to an end event, because the description states an action that must be carried out.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that choosing one of several alternatives, such as accepting one of several arriving alternatives, makes the other still-open alternatives void, so the choice has a consequence for the remaining ones

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that items arrive from an outside source at times the process cannot predict, and that a participant then accepts or denies each arrived item: Model each arrival as its own intermediate catch event, labelled with the arrival itself (for example, the received item plus 'received'), placed on the sequence flow before the participant's decision. Model the accept-or-deny choice as a user task labelled with that decision action, not as a service task, and do not merge the arrival wait into the decision task. Branch on the outcome with an exclusive gateway labelled with a question.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that items arrive from an outside source at times the process cannot predict, and that a participant then accepts or denies each arrived item

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that several distinct actions are carried out in parallel (for example, items are sent in parallel), or that a set of distinct actions must all be completed before the process continues: Model a parallel gateway that forks into one outgoing branch per action, so that all branches start, and a parallel gateway that joins those branches before the next step. Do not model the set as a single task, and do not use an exclusive gateway to merge branches that must all complete.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that several distinct actions are carried out in parallel (for example, items are sent in parallel), or that a set of distinct actions must all be completed before the process continues

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names two or more separate values that a participant enters before a later step, so each value is described on its own: Model each separately named input as its own user task placed in sequence before the later step, and label each task with exactly the input the description names. Do not add inputs, attributes or details that the description does not state, and do not fold unstated items into a task label.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names two or more separate values that a participant enters before a later step, so each value is described on its own
